summary: The FOMC held rates at 3.50-3.75% last week, and markets are now in digestion mode ahead of the April payrolls report due Friday, May 8. Consensus expects just 50,000 jobs added in April, well below March's 178,000, making the print a critical test of whether the labor market is softening fast enough to shift the Fed's calculus. Blowout mega-cap tech earnings last week lifted equities to records, though bond markets remain wary on inflation.
tweet: Fed held, now all eyes on Friday's jobs print — consensus at just 50K — while last week's mega-cap earnings surge keeps stocks at record highs and gold sidelined.
